25 Which radiation could consist of waves of wavelength 0.5 nm?
A
-rays
B
ultraviolet
C
visible light
D
X-rays

hints: Convert the given wavelength to metres: $0.5 \text{ nm} = 0.5 \times 10^{-9} \text{ m} = 5 \times 10^{-10} \text{ m}$.
Recall the order of the electromagnetic spectrum by wavelength and the approximate $400-700 \text{ nm}$ band for visible light and $10-400 \text{ nm}$ band for ultraviolet.
Check whether $5 \times 10^{-10} \text{ m}$ is shorter than ultraviolet and visible light but longer than typical gamma-rays below $10^{-11} \text{ m}$.
walkthrough: Note the given wavelength is $0.5 \text{ nm}$, which is $0.5 \times 10^{-9} \text{ m} = 5 \times 10^{-10} \text{ m}$.

Recall the electromagnetic spectrum in order of decreasing wavelength: visible light is about $4 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$ to $7 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$, ultraviolet is about $10^{-8} \text{ m}$ to $4 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$.
Recall that X-rays are shorter than ultraviolet, roughly $10^{-11} \text{ m}$ to $10^{-8} \text{ m}$, and gamma-rays are still shorter, below about $10^{-11} \text{ m}$.
Compare $5 \times 10^{-10} \text{ m}$ with these ranges: it is much smaller than visible and ultraviolet values but larger than typical gamma-ray wavelengths.
Therefore $0.5 \text{ nm}$ fits the X-ray region. This is option D.

A.explanation: Gamma-rays have much shorter wavelengths, typically less than about $0.01 \text{ nm}$, so $0.5 \text{ nm}$ is too long.

B.explanation: Ultraviolet has wavelengths from about $10 \text{ nm}$ to $400 \text{ nm}$, so $0.5 \text{ nm}$ is shorter than this range.

C.explanation: Visible light has wavelengths from about $400 \text{ nm}$ to $700 \text{ nm}$, almost 1000 times larger than $0.5 \text{ nm}$.

D.explanation: X-rays span roughly $0.01 \text{ nm}$ to $10 \text{ nm}$, so $0.5 \text{ nm}$ lies inside the X-ray region.
